1.why: Reset tokens are stored server-side with a bound userId and originating sessionId, and both `resetRecord` (sessionId check) and `verifiedRecord` (userId/expiry match) enforce that the code belongs to the requesting user's recovery flow.

2.why: A token only validates if `record.sessionId === current.id` and the verified state matches the stored userId, so a code cannot be reused for any other user.

3.why: `/api/reset-complete` only calls `clearVerified()` and rehashes the password; nothing iterates the `sessions` map to revoke other sessions, so pre-existing authenticated sessions remain valid after a reset.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains) is set, but no explicit minVersion/cipher policy is specified, so 'latest TLS' relies solely on Bun defaults.

5.why: Passwords use Argon2id and reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes of 32 random bytes with timing-safe comparisons, though user records themselves live unencrypted in an in-memory Map.

6.why: There is no real email delivery at all — the recovery code, delivery authorization code and MFA code are returned in JSON, printed on the page, and echoed into a visible activity log, so no message-level guarding of private data exists.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated (`validEmail`, `validCode`, `validToken`, `passwordIssue`, 8 KiB body cap, JSON-object-only parsing) and no user input is ever interpolated into HTML or SQL.

8.why: The application performs no redirects whatsoever and CSP sets `form-action 'self'` and `base-uri 'none'`, so there is no open-redirect surface, but the claim is satisfied vacuously rather than by explicit URL whitelisting.

9.why: No email templates exist; the single server-rendered page contains only static markup plus a nonce and JSON-encoded CSRF token, with no user-supplied content reflected.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the recovery token, delivery authorization code and MFA code are deliberately returned to the client and written to the on-page 'Activity logs' and browser console via the overridden `console.log`.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed, but `DELIVERY_AUTHORIZATION_CODE = "864200"`, `MFA_CODE = "246810"` and the demo password `"Initial-Only-Password!42"` are all hardcoded constants in the source.

12.why: A seeded demo account (`helena@hospital.test`) ships with a fixed in-source initial password, and the delivery/MFA codes are static defaults that every user must use.

13.why: `attemptAllowed`/`failedAttempt` enforce MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5 with a 10-minute lockout on login, MFA and delivery authorization, plus a per-context cap on reset requests.

14.why: `/api/reset-request` always returns the same 'If an account is available...' message and issues a token regardless of existence, and login always answers with the generic 'We could not sign you in.'

15.why: The reset code is `randomBytes(32)` hex (64 chars), stored only as a SHA-256 hash, single-use (`record.used`), 15-minute TTL, and bound to a specific userId and sessionId.
